🇮🇷🚢🇺🇸Iran has created a logistical nightmare for the U.S. Navy

The New York Times reports that sustaining America’s massive naval deployment against Iran is becoming an increasingly difficult logistical operation.

Around 20 U.S. warships carrying roughly 20,000 sailors and Marines require more than 420,000 meals and approximately 8 MILLION gallons of fuel every week.

Iran’s destruction of a critical U.S. Navy logistics base in Bahrain, combined with the vulnerability of other regional ports to Iranian missiles and drones, has deprived the fleet of its nearby logistics network. 

Supply ships are now forced to travel approximately 2,200 miles to Diego Garcia, or potentially 3,700 miles to Singapore, before returning to replenish U.S. warships operating in the Arabian Sea and Gulf of Oman.

Navy chief Adm. Daryl Caudle acknowledged this week that personnel “aren’t getting back” to Bahrain anytime soon, while the Navy has been grappling with exceptionally long deployments and disrupted supply chains.
